subject: docs/coop/artifacts/coordinator-decisions.D-099.draft.md
summary: D-099 is a lawful new cycle and preserves the substantive D-098 turn-3 repairs: exactly five operative G03 quantities, paired current-VM regression measurements from release two onward, no weekly-image rebaseline, unchanged D-006 numerals, explicit G04 series, and complete rollback. It also removes `/proc/self/exe` and universal-binary slice ambiguity. One SHOULD-FIX remains. The replacement still does not define a deterministic observation of the successfully exec'd target process: Linux `file -L /proc/T/exe` reads executable metadata and can race a pre-exec wrapper, target exit, or PID reuse; macOS declares the requested `arch` value to be process architecture and permits translation to be read from a helper rather than from the target. No same-PID exec handshake, target identity binding, liveness protocol, normalized observed output, or short-lived-command race handling is specified. The fail-closed architecture proof therefore remains incomplete, so CONSENT and the proposed condition-4 MET transition are unavailable.

objections.title: The replacement still infers target-process state without an exec/liveness identity protocol
objections.finding: Lines 30-43 correct the inspector path and ban fat binaries, but they do not establish when PID T has successfully exec'd the digest-pinned target or keep that short-lived process observable. On Linux, `/proc/T/exe` is a link to the executed program and `file` opens that executable; its output is executable format metadata, not a distinct runtime-ABI observation. Without a post-exec handshake and target identity check, the read may see a launcher/helper, fail after `--help` or `--version` exits, or be attempted after PID reuse. On macOS, `arch -arm64` / `arch -x86_64` is an architecture-selection request, yet the draft simply defines the request as the process result. The documented `arch` behavior may try a close match when the requested architecture is unavailable. The alternative `sysctl.proc_translated` result comes from a helper process unless an optional, undefined target command happens to exist; Apple defines that sysctl as reporting whether the calling process is translated. 'Same arch immediately before' is not an explicit same-PID, same-exec-image evidence binding. Thin artifacts make the intended result plausible but do not turn these inferences into the claimed independently recorded host/executable/process facts.
evidence: D-099 lines 30-43 name PID T but specify no command/arguments, child-stop or post-exec handshake, PID start-time/path/digest identity check, liveness rule, or behavior when a short-lived target exits before inspection.
Linux kernel procfs documentation says `/proc/<pid>/exe` is a link to the executable and warns that a PID may be reused after exit: https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/v6.8/filesystems/proc.html .
Linux proc_pid_exe documentation says dereferencing `/proc/<pid>/exe` opens the executable and that the link can become unavailable: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/proc_pid_exe.5.html .

The macOS `arch` contract is selection-order control, not a target-process query, and may select a close match when the requested architecture is absent: https://keith.github.io/xcode-man-pages/arch.1.html .

Apple documents `sysctl.proc_translated` as a call made by the process whose Rosetta state is being determined: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/Apple-Silicon/about-the-rosetta-translation-environment .
objections.impact: An implementation can record a launcher or executable-format result as the target process fact, or reject nondeterministically because the bounded startup command has already exited. The helper-based macOS branch proves the helper's translation state rather than retaining evidence from the target itself. That falls short of the fail-closed, reproducible no-silent-Rosetta/process-architecture contract needed to name G03/G04 and mark condition 4 MET.
objections.requiredRepair: Specify one deterministic target-bound protocol per OS. Bind PID plus process start identity to the exact digest-pinned executable; prove successful exec before observation; hold or instrument the child so the observation cannot race `--help`/`--version` exit; define the exact observed field, normalized accepted values, and failure behavior. On Linux, do not count `file` of `/proc/<T>/exe` as both executable and process facts without an additional target-specific ABI observation. On macOS, require the target itself to return normalized architecture and `sysctl.proc_translated` state, or define a documented target-PID mechanism; if a same-process pre-exec helper is retained, require same PID, exact exec target/digest, no intervening fork, and an explicit proof that the reported property survives that exact exec. Clarify whether the thin-only rule constrains shipped release artifacts or only a digest-bound measurement projection. Refreeze for turn 2.

predecessorFindingDisposition.ADV-D098-T3-01: PARTIALLY RESOLVED. D-099 replaces `/proc/self/exe` with `/proc/T/exe`, captures a target PID, rejects fat/universal artifacts, and avoids using an unrelated default-architecture `sysctl` command. It does not land the required target ABI observation, exact fields/normalization, or lifetime/race handling, and its macOS helper is not explicitly bound to the target process. The residual is ADV-D099-01.
